prompt:
Write 9 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a low-speed head-on collision claim, in time order. Injury: back strain. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1500; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- It is not clear whether all of the damage came from this impact.
- The claimant later added small details, but the account stayed the same.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- A few old scratches may be older than this crash.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: First notice of loss received from the insured's policyholder regarding a low-speed head-on collision. The claimant reports a back strain and is represented by counsel, so all further contact will go through the attorney's office.

Entry 2: Verified the driver is named on the policy and that coverage was in force at the time of the loss. Nothing in the file suggests the damage predates the policy start.

Entry 3: Police report obtained. It confirms the claimant was in the vehicle at the time of impact, and the responding officer's account matches the insured's description of the collision.

Entry 4: Statements taken from two witnesses and the other driver. All three describe the accident the same way as the insured, and scene photos are consistent with that account.

Entry 5: Vehicle inspection completed. The impact damage fits a low-speed head-on collision. A few older scratches are visible on the bumper, and it is not yet clear whether all of the damage came from this impact, so a repair estimate is pending a closer look.

Entry 6: Medical records received from the claimant's treating provider. The reported back strain fits the kind and force of this crash well, and no prior injury to the same body area is known.

Entry 7: Claimant's attorney sent a supplemental statement adding a few small details about the moment of impact. The core account is unchanged from the initial report.

Entry 8: Treatment records show a usual course of care that tapered off as the patient improved. Requested updated provider notes to confirm current status and whether any further treatment is expected.

Entry 9: File reviewed with the claimant's counsel in place. Next steps are to finalize the repair estimate, reconcile the older scratches against the impact damage, and reassess the bodily injury claim once the latest treatment notes arrive.
